claims.text: Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi exhibits a coarse microstructure.
Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi exhibits detectable elemental segregation.
Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi has high residual thermal stresses.
Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi has a substantial defect population.
Increasing L-PBF scanning speed refines the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
High-speed L-PBF produces a uniformly distributed grain structure in AlCrFeNiSi.
Increasing L-PBF scanning speed suppresses elemental segregation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Increasing L-PBF scanning speed reduces thermally induced residual stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
Faster laser scanning produces higher solidification cooling rates.
Higher cooling rates restrict the time available for elemental diffusion and aggregation.
Rapid solidification minimizes dendritic formation and segregation.
Rapid solidification reduces residual thermal gradients.
Rapid solidification limits defect formation, including hot cracking.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defect formation enhance overall mechanical performance.
High-scanning-speed AlCrFeNiSi parts will have greater tensile strength than slower-scan parts.
High-scanning-speed AlCrFeNiSi parts will have greater ductility than slower-scan parts.
High-scanning-speed AlCrFeNiSi parts will have lower residual stress than slower-scan parts.
High-scanning-speed AlCrFeNiSi parts will contain fewer microstructural defects than slower-scan parts.
The proposed effect holds within the volumetric-energy-density window typical of powder-based additive manufacturing of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed results may not translate to substantially different alloy systems or fabrication processes.

contradictions.description: The conditions call for controlled volumetric energy density, but the experiment changes scanning speed while holding laser power, hatch spacing, and layer thickness constant. Under the standard L-PBF energy-density relation, this necessarily changes volumetric energy density, so scanning speed is not isolated from energy input.

The hypothesis and experiment use slower-scan L-PBF as the comparator, whereas the baseline also includes bulk fabrication. These are distinct baselines with different thermal histories, making the stated relative outcome ambiguous.
